question.:question/problem: If the path $C$ is the line segment $\overset{―}{MN}$ traversed from the point $M(-1,0)$ to the point $N(2,4),$ then ${\int }_{C}y\,dx-x\,dy=$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The position vectors of the endpoints of our line segment are $a=-i$ and $b=2\,i+4\,j.$ So, the parametrization of the line segment is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =a+t\,(b-a) \\  & =-i+t(2\,i+4\,j-(-i)) \\  & =-i+t(3\,i+4\,j) \\  & =(3t-1)\,i+4t\,j,\end{aligned}
$$

where $0\le t\le 1.$ Thus, we have that $x(t)=3t-1$ and $y(t)=4t$ along the segment.

The derivative of $r(t)$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j=3\,i+4\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

We can now evaluate the line integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}y\,dx-x\,dy & ={\int }_{0}^{1}y\,\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t-x\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(y\,\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}-x\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})dt \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}4t(3)-(3t-1)(4)\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}4\,dt \\  & =4t\,{|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =4(1-0) \\  & =4\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: If the path $C$ is the line segment $\overset{―}{MN}$ traversed from the point $M(0,1)$ to the point $N(3,3),$ then ${\int }_{C}{x}^{2}\,dx-y\,dy=$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The position vectors of the endpoints of our line segment are $a=j$ and $b=3\,i+3\,j.$ So, the parametrization of the line segment is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =a+t\,(b-a) \\  & =j+t(3\,i+3\,j-j) \\  & =j+t(3\,i+2\,j) \\  & =3t\,i+(1+2t)\,j,\end{aligned}
$$

where $0\le t\le 1.$ Thus, we have that $x(t)=3t$ and $y(t)=1+2t$ along the segment.

The derivative of $r(t)$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j=3\,i+2\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

We can now evaluate the line integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}{x}^{2}\,dx-y\,dy & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{2}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t-y\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}({x}^{2}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}-y\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(3t)^{2}\cdot 3-(1+2t)\cdot 2\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}27{t}^{2}-2-4t\,dt \\  & ={[9{t}^{3}-2t-2{t}^{2}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =[9(1)^{3}-2(1)-2(1)^{2}]-[0] \\  & =5\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: If the path $C$ is the line segment $\overset{―}{AB}$ traversed from the point $A(-1,2)$ to the point $B(1,0),$ then ${\int }_{C}xy\,dx+dy=$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The position vectors of the endpoints of our line segment are $a=-i+2\,j$ and $b=i.$ So, the parametrization of the line segment is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =a+t\,(b-a) \\  & =-i+2\,j+t(i-(-i+2\,j)) \\  & =-i+2\,j+t(2\,i-2\,j) \\  & =(2t-1)\,i+(2-2t)\,j,\end{aligned}
$$

where $0\le t\le 1.$ Thus, we have that $x(t)=2t-1$ and $y(t)=2-2t$ along the segment.

The derivative of $r(t)$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j=2\,i-2\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

We can now evaluate the line integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}xy\,dx+dy & ={\int }_{0}^{1}xy\,\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(xy\,\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})dt \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(2t-1)(2-2t)(2)+(-2)\,dt \\  & =2{\int }_{0}^{1}(2t-1)(2-2t)-1\,dt \\  & =2{\int }_{0}^{1}-4{t}^{2}+6t-3\,dt \\  & =2{[-\frac{4{t}^{3}}{3}+3{t}^{2}-3t]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =2[-\frac{4}{3}+3-3]-2[0] \\  & =2[-\frac{4}{3}] \\  & =-\frac{8}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: If the path $C$ is the line segment $\overset{―}{AB}$ traversed from the point $A(0,0)$ to the point $B(4,2),$ then ${\int }_{C}{e}^{x+y}\,dx-{e}^{x+y}\,dy=$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The position vectors of the endpoints of our line segment are $a=0\,i+0\,j$ and $b=4\,i+2\,j.$ So, the parametrization of the line segment is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =a+t\,(b-a) \\  & =0\,i+0\,j+t(4\,i+2\,j-(0\,i+0\,j)) \\  & =4t\,i+2t\,j,\end{aligned}
$$

where $0\le t\le 1.$ Thus, we have that $x(t)=4t$ and $y(t)=2t$ along the segment.

The derivative of $r(t)$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j=4\,i+2\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

We can now evaluate the line integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}{e}^{x+y}\,dx-{e}^{x+y}\,dy & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{e}^{x+y}\,\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t-{e}^{x+y}\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{e}^{x+y}(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}-\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{e}^{4t+2t}(4-2)\,\text{d}t \\  & =2{\int }_{0}^{1}{e}^{6t}\,\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{{e}^{6t}}{3}\,{|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{6(1)}}{3}-\frac{{e}^{6(0)}}{3} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{6}}{3}-\frac{1}{3} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{6}-1}{3}\end{aligned}

$$

$$

where $0\le t\le 1.$ Thus, we have that $x(t)=4 - 4 t$ and $y(t)=2 - t$ along the segment.

The derivative of $r(t)$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{\prime}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j=-4\,i-j.\end{aligned}
$$

We can now evaluate the line integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_C \left(- x\right)\,dx+\left(- 2 x y\right)\,dy & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\left(- x\right)\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+\left(- 2 x y\right)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,dt \\   & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\left(\left(- x\right)\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+\left(- 2 x y\right)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\right)\,dt \\   & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\left(-1\right)\cdot \left(4 - 4 t\right)\cdot \left(-4\right)+\left(-2\right)\cdot \left(4 - 4 t\right)\cdot \left(2 - t\right)\cdot \left(-1\right)\,dt \\   & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\left(16 - 16 t\right)+\left(8 t^{2} - 24 t + 16\right)\,dt \\   & ={\int }_{0}^{1}8 t^{2} - 40 t + 32\,dt \\   & =\left[\frac{8 t^{3}}{3} - 20 t^{2} + 32 t\right]_0^1 \\   & =\left(\frac{8 \left(1\right)^{3}}{3} - 20 \left(1\right)^{2} + 32 \left(1\right)\right)-\left(\frac{8 \left(0\right)^{3}}{3} - 20 \left(0\right)^{2} + 32 \left(0\right)\right) \\   & =\left(\left(\frac{8}{3}\right)+\left(-20\right)+\left(32\right)\right)-\left(\left(0\right)+\left(0\right)+\left(0\right)\right) \\   & =\frac{44}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

\begin{aligned}{\int }_C \left(- 3 x^{2} y\right)\,dx+\left(- 3 x y^{2}\right)\,dy & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\left(- 3 x^{2} y\right)\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+\left(- 3 x y^{2}\right)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,dt \\   & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\left(\left(- 3 x^{2} y\right)\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+\left(- 3 x y^{2}\right)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\right)\,dt \\   & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\left(-3\right)\cdot \left(2 t - 2\right)^{2}\cdot \left(3 t - 3\right)\cdot \left(2\right)+\left(-3\right)\cdot \left(2 t - 2\right)\cdot \left(3 t - 3\right)^{2}\cdot \left(3\right)\,dt \\   & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\left(- 72 t^{3} + 216 t^{2} - 216 t + 72\right)+\left(- 162 t^{3} + 486 t^{2} - 486 t + 162\right)\,dt \\   & ={\int }_{0}^{1}- 234 t^{3} + 702 t^{2} - 702 t + 234\,dt \\   & =\left[- \frac{117 t^{4}}{2} + 234 t^{3} - 351 t^{2} + 234 t\right]_0^1 \\   & =\left(- \frac{117 \left(1\right)^{4}}{2} + 234 \left(1\right)^{3} - 351 \left(1\right)^{2} + 234 \left(1\right)\right)-\left(- \frac{117 \left(0\right)^{4}}{2} + 234 \left(0\right)^{3} - 351 \left(0\right)^{2} + 234 \left(0\right)\right) \\   & =\left(\left(- \frac{117}{2}\right)+\left(234\right)+\left(-351\right)+\left(234\right)\right)-\left(\left(0\right)+\left(0\right)+\left(0\right)+\left(0\right)\right) \\   & =\frac{117}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: If the path $C$ is the line segment $\overline{AB}$ traversed from the point $A(-2,2)$ to the point $B(-3,0),$ then ${\int }_C \left(3 x^{2} y\right)\,dx+\left(x y^{2}\right)\,dy=$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The position vectors of the endpoints of our line segment are $a=-2\,i+2\,j$ and $b=-3\,i.$ So, the parametrization of the line segment is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =a+t\,(b-a) \\   & =-2\,i+2\,j+t\left(-3\,i-\left(-2\,i+2\,j\right)\right) \\   & =-2\,i+2\,j+t\left(-i-2\,j\right) \\   & =\left(- t - 2\right)\,i+\left(2 - 2 t\right)\,j,\end{aligned}
$$

where $0\le t\le 1.$ Thus, we have that $x(t)=- t - 2$ and $y(t)=2 - 2 t$ along the segment.

The derivative of $r(t)$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{\prime}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j=-i-2\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

We can now evaluate the line integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_C \left(3 x^{2} y\right)\,dx+\left(x y^{2}\right)\,dy & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\left(3 x^{2} y\right)\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+\left(x y^{2}\right)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,dt \\   & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\left(\left(3 x^{2} y\right)\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+\left(x y^{2}\right)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\right)\,dt \\   & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\left(3\right)\cdot \left(- t - 2\right)^{2}\cdot \left(2 - 2 t\right)\cdot \left(-1\right)+\left(1\right)\cdot \left(- t - 2\right)\cdot \left(2 - 2 t\right)^{2}\cdot \left(-2\right)\,dt \\   & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\left(6 t^{3} + 18 t^{2} - 24\right)+\left(8 t^{3} - 24 t + 16\right)\,dt \\   & ={\int }_{0}^{1}14 t^{3} + 18 t^{2} - 24 t - 8\,dt \\   & =\left[\frac{7 t^{4}}{2} + 6 t^{3} - 12 t^{2} - 8 t\right]_0^1 \\   & =\left(\frac{7 \left(1\right)^{4}}{2} + 6 \left(1\right)^{3} - 12 \left(1\right)^{2} - 8 \left(1\right)\right)-\left(\frac{7 \left(0\right)^{4}}{2} + 6 \left(0\right)^{3} - 12 \left(0\right)^{2} - 8 \left(0\right)\right) \\   & =\left(\left(\frac{7}{2}\right)+\left(6\right)+\left(-12\right)+\left(-8\right)\right)-\left(\left(0\right)+\left(0\right)+\left(0\right)+\left(0\right)\right) \\   & =- \frac{21}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: If the path $C$ is the line segment $\overline{AB}$ traversed from the point $A(-2,-2)$ to the point $B(-3,1),$ then ${\int }_C \left(x^{2} y\right)\,dx+\left(- 2 x y^{2}\right)\,dy=$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The position vectors of the endpoints of our line segment are $a=-2\,i-2\,j$ and $b=-3\,i+j.$ So, the parametrization of the line segment is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =a+t\,(b-a) \\   & =-2\,i-2\,j+t\left(-3\,i+j-\left(-2\,i-2\,j\right)\right) \\   & =-2\,i-2\,j+t\left(-i+3\,j\right) \\   & =\left(- t - 2\right)\,i+\left(3 t - 2\right)\,j,\end{aligned}
$$

where $0\le t\le 1.$ Thus, we have that $x(t)=- t - 2$ and $y(t)=3 t - 2$ along the segment.

The derivative of $r(t)$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{\prime}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j=-i+3\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

We can now evaluate the line integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_C \left(x^{2} y\right)\,dx+\left(- 2 x y^{2}\right)\,dy & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\left(x^{2} y\right)\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+\left(- 2 x y^{2}\right)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,dt \\   & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\left(\left(x^{2} y\right)\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+\left(- 2 x y^{2}\right)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\right)\,dt \\   & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\left(1\right)\cdot \left(- t - 2\right)^{2}\cdot \left(3 t - 2\right)\cdot \left(-1\right)+\left(-2\right)\cdot \left(- t - 2\right)\cdot \left(3 t - 2\right)^{2}\cdot \left(3\right)\,dt \\   & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\left(- 3 t^{3} - 10 t^{2} - 4 t + 8\right)+\left(54 t^{3} + 36 t^{2} - 120 t + 48\right)\,dt \\   & ={\int }_{0}^{1}51 t^{3} + 26 t^{2} - 124 t + 56\,dt \\   & =\left[\frac{51 t^{4}}{4} + \frac{26 t^{3}}{3} - 62 t^{2} + 56 t\right]_0^1 \\   & =\left(\frac{51 \left(1\right)^{4}}{4} + \frac{26 \left(1\right)^{3}}{3} - 62 \left(1\right)^{2} + 56 \left(1\right)\right)-\left(\frac{51 \left(0\right)^{4}}{4} + \frac{26 \left(0\right)^{3}}{3} - 62 \left(0\right)^{2} + 56 \left(0\right)\right) \\   & =\left(\left(\frac{51}{4}\right)+\left(\frac{26}{3}\right)+\left(-62\right)+\left(56\right)\right)-\left(\left(0\right)+\left(0\right)+\left(0\right)+\left(0\right)\right) \\   & =\frac{185}{12}\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: If the path $C$ is the line segment $\overline{AB}$ traversed from the point $A(2,-2)$ to the point $B(-1,0),$ then ${\int }_C \left(- 3 x^{2} y\right)\,dx+\left(- 2 x y^{2}\right)\,dy=$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The position vectors of the endpoints of our line segment are $a=2\,i-2\,j$ and $b=-i.$ So, the parametrization of the line segment is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =a+t\,(b-a) \\   & =2\,i-2\,j+t\left(-i-\left(2\,i-2\,j\right)\right) \\   & =2\,i-2\,j+t\left(-3\,i+2\,j\right) \\   & =\left(2 - 3 t\right)\,i+\left(2 t - 2\right)\,j,\end{aligned}
$$

where $0\le t\le 1.$ Thus, we have that $x(t)=2 - 3 t$ and $y(t)=2 t - 2$ along the segment.

The derivative of $r(t)$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{\prime}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j=-3\,i+2\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

We can now evaluate the line integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_C \left(- 3 x^{2} y\right)\,dx+\left(- 2 x y^{2}\right)\,dy & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\left(- 3 x^{2} y\right)\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+\left(- 2 x y^{2}\right)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,dt \\   & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\left(\left(- 3 x^{2} y\right)\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+\left(- 2 x y^{2}\right)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\right)\,dt \\   & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\left(-3\right)\cdot \left(2 - 3 t\right)^{2}\cdot \left(2 t - 2\right)\cdot \left(-3\right)+\left(-2\right)\cdot \left(2 - 3 t\right)\cdot \left(2 t - 2\right)^{2}\cdot \left(2\right)\,dt \\   & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\left(162 t^{3} - 378 t^{2} + 288 t - 72\right)+\left(48 t^{3} - 128 t^{2} + 112 t - 32\right)\,dt \\   & ={\int }_{0}^{1}210 t^{3} - 506 t^{2} + 400 t - 104\,dt \\   & =\left[\frac{105 t^{4}}{2} - \frac{506 t^{3}}{3} + 200 t^{2} - 104 t\right]_0^1 \\   & =\left(\frac{105 \left(1\right)^{4}}{2} - \frac{506 \left(1\right)^{3}}{3} + 200 \left(1\right)^{2} - 104 \left(1\right)\right)-\left(\frac{105 \left(0\right)^{4}}{2} - \frac{506 \left(0\right)^{3}}{3} + 200 \left(0\right)^{2} - 104 \left(0\right)\right) \\   & =\left(\left(\frac{105}{2}\right)+\left(- \frac{506}{3}\right)+\left(200\right)+\left(-104\right)\right)-\left(\left(0\right)+\left(0\right)+\left(0\right)+\left(0\right)\right) \\   & =- \frac{121}{6}\end{aligned}
$$
